title: Por and Para in Time and Space

sections.content:
Time and space highlight the classic contrast between **por** and **para**:

1. **Time Deadline** (*para*): *El informe es para el lunes.* (Due by Monday)
2. **Time Duration** (*por*): *Estudié por tres horas.* (Duration of 3 hours)
3. **Time of day** (*por*): *por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche*
4. **Motion through a place** (*por*): *Caminamos por el parque.* (Through / around the park)
5. **Motion toward a place** (*para*): *Vamos para casa.* (Heading home)

sections.title: Key Patterns
rows: Esperamos por dos horas en la estación.

items.english: I need the car ready by Friday.

items.spanish: El gato escapó por la ventana.
items.english: The cat escaped through the window.

sections.content: *Para* sets a cutoff point or final stop; *por* covers the duration elapsed or the area traveled through.
